E2.reason: Pure in-process asyncio scheduling. Worker.run() creates the run-loop task and awaits asyncio.shield(loop_task); a cancellation landing before that task's first step calls stop(), and the task's first statement (_stop_event.clear() at the top of _run_loop) erases it. Read in the parent (896abfd worker.py run/_run_loop): no database statement lies between create_task and the loop task's first step (prune_stalled_workers and register_worker complete before it; a cancellation during them raises at that await and is not lost). The database does not mediate the defect; the maintainers' regression test (tests/unit/test_worker.py::test_stop_requested_before_run_loop_starts_is_not_lost) replaces Worker._run_loop and runs on the in-memory test app.

E2.reason: In-process worker shutdown logic. The change renames shutdown_timeout to shutdown_graceful_timeout, replaces asyncio.wait_for on the loop task with asyncio.wait on the running job tasks, adds AbortReason (USER_REQUEST/SHUTDOWN) to JobContext so a sync job (run in a thread) can see a shutdown abort through should_abort(), and lets a shutdown-aborted job be retried. The behaviour is decided by Python timers, thread-run sync jobs and the worker's in-memory abort map; the database only records the resulting status. The maintainers' acceptance tests drive it with wall-clock sleeps (0.05 s) and a 0.3 s graceful timeout.
